1. Industry Overview

In general, Commodity Codes are a tool to classify goods or services. A Commodity Code provides a standardized Code and General Description of the goods or services being purchased that can be used in a variety of ways within Procurement, such as; workflow routing, sourcing routing, procurement analysis, automatic account code assignment and with inventory and forecasting systems.

sections.title: Are Commodity Codes just a JAGGAER “thing”?
paragraphs: No. Most all ERPs have a “standardized code” tool available for classification of goods or services. It could be named different i.e. categories or commodity, but the function is the same and often they are “required” on requisitions.

sections.title: Where do these “standardized codes” come from, and how do they get assigned to goods or services?
paragraphs: The two most common standards are UNSPSC and NIGP (summarized below). How they are assigned to goods or services depends… They can be manually assigned at the time of purchase, but more commonly the Supplier categorizes their items with one of these standard codes which is then “mapped” to a Commodity Code and applied to an item automatically.

1. UNSPSC (United Nations Standard Products and Services Code) UNSPSC is a coding system for the classification of both products and services for use throughout the global marketplace. It is managed by the GS1 US, which is responsible for overseeing code change requests, revising the codes by interfacing with industry projects and issuing regularly scheduled updates to the code.

2. NIGP (National Institute of Governmental Purchasing – Commodity/Services Code) The NIGP Code is a coding taxonomy used primarily to classify products and services procured by state and local governments.

sections.title: How do Companies decide what standard to use and how is “mapping” used?
paragraphs: Most companies determine a standard, a Commodity Code structure and mapping based on their business sector, procurement policies, ERP/Procurement systems capabilities and the functionality they desire.

Mapping allows the thousands of categorized goods and services to be mapped to a higher level Commodity Code. Most companies don’t need granularity down to the lowest category, so they map the lower categories up to a higher “general” level category.

Companies can choose to have their system Commodity Codes based on the standard they use i.e. UNSPSC based Commodity Codes where their Commodity Codes/Descriptions mirror the UNSPSC standard or they may choose to create their own Commodity Codes/Descriptions specific to their company.

Depending on the granularity of categorization the Company desires they could have thousands of Commodity Codes or just a handful. They could be; UNSPSC based, NGIP based or internally created Commodity Codes.
1. JAGGAER Commodity Code Overview

The “mapping” of items within JAGGAER ePro to a Client Commodity Code is actual the last step in a somewhat complicated process, luckily most of that process is automated through the JAGGAER Taxonomy.

The JAGGAER Taxonomy ensures that the hundreds of thousands of items (from hundreds of Suppliers) can all be categorized based on information that the Supplier has given us for the item. Since the JAGGAER Taxonomy is UNSPSC based, each item has to be assigned a corresponding UNSPSC. Based on our Clients, current industry standards and the current UNSPSC version JAGGAER determines which UNSPSC is assigned to which JAGGAER Category (Category Assigned UNSPSC Codes) and what UNSPSCs are included in our Taxonomy.

JAGGAER ePro Items that have successfully traversed the JAGGAER Taxonomy will have a Category Assigned UNSPSC Code (as well as a JAGGAER Category for Hosted Items) and will be willing and ready to be mapped to a Client Commodity Code.

sections.title: JAGGAER Taxonomy
paragraphs: The JAGGAER Taxonomy is based on two hierarchies; a Proprietary hierarchy for scientific products and a UNSPSC hierarchy for non-scientific products.
Each of these hierarchies is broken into multiple categories; each category is:
1. Assigned an “JAGGAER determined” UNSPSC code
2. Assigned to a JAGGAER Vertical (unrelated to Taxonomy/Commodity Codes)
JAGGAER Taxonomy Notes:
The Proprietary Hierarchy is primarily used for “SciCat” Suppliers.
Not all UNSPSC Codes are included in the JAGGAER Taxonomy, there are thousands omitted based on our Supplier base.

The JAGGAER Taxonomy is reviewed periodically and updated as needed based the current UNSPSC Version or if UNSPSCs need to be included in the Taxonomy. Updates typically coincide with a major JAGGAER Release.

sections.title: How the JAGGAER Taxonomy is applied to JAGGAER ePro items
paragraphs: Hosted Suppliers must provide either a “JAGGAER Category” or “UNSPSC” when loading their hosted content:
1. If the JAGGAER “Category” is given, the item will be assigned the corresponding Category Assigned UNSPSC Code.
2. If the UNSPSC is given, the item will be assigned the JAGGAER “Category” for the corresponding Category Assigned UNSPSC Code.
Punch-out Suppliers only return a UNSPSC (no JAGGAER Category):
1. The UNSPSC returned by the Supplier is matched to a Category Assigned UNSPSC Code.
Note:
Some punch-out Suppliers can be problematic in regards to the JAGGAER Taxonomy if their items have UNSPSC assignments that are out of date (old UNSPSC Version) or contain no UNSPSC assignment.
1. JAGGAER Commodity Code Mapping – The “Nitty -Gritty”
Important Considerations:

Commodity Codes should be kept to the high level possible. This is especially relevant for non-Cat Items & forms or if the Client will NOT be auto-applying CC’s to items. In these cases Users will have to manually choose a CC, when faced with a huge list, they typically choose the first one regardless of the item.
Example: Client wants to implement UNSPSC based Commodity Codes.
There are nearly 19,000 Category Assigned UNSPSC Codes in the JAGGAER Taxonomy
How efficient would it be to have 19,000 or even 1,000 Commodity Codes?
Does the client really need granularity down to “Infants overshoes”?
If not, a higher level of “Footwear” or better yet an even higher level of “Apparel and Luggage and Personal Care Products” might suffice.
A basic UNSPSC based Commodity Code structure based on the highest UNSPSC level (Segment) will yield approximately 55 Commodity Codes on ePro

sections.title: Set the Mapping Configuration and Import the Mapping
paragraphs: Now that you have your Commodity Codes loaded on ePro the next step is to determine how to “Map” them.

sections.title: Step 1: Commodity Code Configuration
paragraphs: The settings below determine the base mapping configuration, these must be set before “mapping” can begin. Configure these settings based on the Client’s desired functionality as determined by the questions previously discussed here: Things to know before beginning the Commodity Code & Mapping process on Page 4

headers: Select to use category mapping functionality
Checking this box enables mapping of organization values for categories/commodities to the JAGGAER taxonomy and exposes the “Mapping Values” section
rows: Mapping Type
Category Name*
This option maps the Commodity Code field to the JAGGAER Category Name. Mapped values can be overridden on the Category Map tab.
Category UN/SPSC*

This option maps the Commodity Code field to the JAGGAER Category UN/SPSC values. Mapped values can be overridden on the Category Map tab. (Setting for the display of UN/SPSC values are set on the UN/SPSC Settings tab.)
Free-Form Value**
This option does not map the Commodity Code field to any value by default. Mappings must be explicitly set up through the UI or by importing them.

Value List**
(MOST COMMON)

This option does not map the Commodity Code field to any value by default. Mappings must be explicitly set up through the UI or by importing them. The values for mapping are those defined on the Manage Value List tab.

* This option does not use inheritance for mappings, i.e., child categories do not inherit their parent's mapping value, and each category mapping must be explicitly overridden.

Automatically populate Commodity Code values in cart

If the Commodity Code field in the Shopping Cart is to be automatically populated when an item is added to the shopping cart, select this option. When selected, additional options appear to configure which rules are to be used to populate the Commodity Code field.
Use category mapped values

This rule, if selected, is the first one applied for populating the Commodity Code field when an item is added to the Shopping Cart.
For hosted catalog items, the value mapped on the Category Map tab is used. If a mapped value does not exist, the next rule is applied.
For PunchOut items, the system attempts to match the UN/SPSC number provided by the PunchOut vendor for the item to one of the values in the JAGGAER taxonomy. If the UN/SPSC value is found, the mapped value is used. If a mapped value does not exist or If the system cannot map the UN/SPSC value for the item the next rule is used.
Use supplier master commodity code values

This rule, if selected, is applied after the category mapping rule (assuming it is selected.) If a category mapping does not exist, the Commodity Code value defined for the supplier in the supplier master is used. If one does not exist, the next rule is applied.
If no category/commodity code available, use
If none of the prior rules populate the Commodity Code field, the value defined here is used.

headers: Allow users to modify value in cart

If users are to be allowed to override Commodity Code values that auto-populated, select this option. The Commodity Code field is free-form for mapping types other than Value List. For value List, the field is a pull-down if there are 50 or fewer values, and it is a free-form for greater than 50 values. If free-form, the value is validated against the defined list.
rows: Show commodity code description (Value List only)

This setting will determine whether or not commodity code description is shown on a requisition, PO, or invoice. If the box is not checked, the commodity code will be displayed with no description. This will not impact the ability to search on description if the commodity code search is being utilized.
Show commodity description in selection drop-down box (Value List only)

This option adds the commodity code description to the drop-down selection box on the document. If the number of commodity code values is less than the organization search threshold then the commodity code values are displayed in a drop-down selection box. Please note that only the first 40 characters will be displayed in the selection box, which includes the value.
Sort commodity code values by description
Sorts the selection of Commodity Codes by description as opposed to value.
Map Commodity Codes to Custom Field Values (Value List only)

For the Value List Mapping Type, you may select an active Custom Field to use in mapping commodity codes to specific custom field values. Once you have selected a custom field, you may select commodity codes to map a custom field value.
Note: For a custom field value to be applied to the mapped commodity code, the custom field and value must be active, and placed in the codes section (header and line level) on the requisition document configuration.
SCT ONLY - Use Commodity Code field in integration
For Banner Customers only: Uses the Commodity Code Field for Banner Integrations

sections.title: Verify the Configuration and Mapping
paragraphs: You’ve done it! Commodity Code structure has been determined, Commodity Codes have been loaded, configuration has been set & the values have been mapped. All that’s left now is to verify everything is correct

Things don’t seem right? Need to do some debugging? See APPENDIX B – Debugging: Tips/Tricks & Secrets08D0C9EA79F9BACE118C8200AA004BA90B02000000080000000E0000005F005200650066003400300031003500370037003700330031000000 , hopefully it will help…

headers: Steps
What am I looking for?
rows: Go to the “Category Map”
Perform a cursory check of your mapping. Do you have the applicable Overridden Indicator and associated Client Commodity Code? Open some tree sub-categories; are they inheriting as expected?
Were Commodity Codes automatically applied to ePro Hosted/Punch-out items?
If so, add some hosted items to your cart. Is the CC automatically applied? Is it “mapped” correctly? Check a punch-out item as well.
Were Users allowed to modify Commodity Codes in their Cart?
If so, the auto-applied Commodity Code in the cart should be editable by the User.
Were Commodity Codes used for workflow routing?
If you imported/set-up CC Dynamic Workflow, then you better check a few Rules. For an applicable CC in your Cart/PR is it routing properly (check Approvals tab).
Were Commodity Codes “required” on the Cart/Requisition?
If so, either delete the CC in the cart (if you are allowed) or find an item that doesn’t have a CC mapped. It should Error or Warn on Checkout depending on your PR Doc setting for the CC Field.
Were Commodity Codes “mapped” to a Custom Field?

If so, verify that for the applicable CC, the associated custom field is either populated (if defaulted) of the choices are limited to the mapped values. Note: Mapping only applies to the Cart /Requisition.
Were “Use Supplier Master CC Values” or “if no category/CC available” Used?

Check you mapping Hierarchy:
Use Mapped Value – If none then…
Use Supplier Master (on Supplier Profile) – If none then…
Use the defined catch-all CC
